questions.questionText: When did World War II begin and end?
questions.explanation: WWII began with German invasion of Poland in 1939 and ended with Japanese surrender in 1945.

questions.questionText: What was the Holocaust?

options.text: Nazi genocide of six million Jews

questions.explanation: Holocaust was Nazi systematic murder of 6 million Jews and millions of others in death camps.

questions.questionText: Who were the Allied Powers in WWII?
questions.explanation: Allied Powers (Britain, Soviet Union, US, China, Free French) defeated Axis Powers.

questions.questionText: What was the D-Day invasion?

options.text: Allied landing in Normandy to open Western Front

questions.explanation: D-Day (June 6, 1944) was largest amphibious invasion, opening second front in Europe.

questions.questionText: Who was Winston Churchill?

options.text: British Prime Minister leading war effort

questions.explanation: Churchill led Britain throughout WWII, inspiring resistance against Nazi Germany.

questions.questionText: What was the Battle of Stalingrad?

options.text: Decisive Soviet victory turning point in Eastern Front

questions.explanation: Stalingrad was brutal urban warfare culminating in German surrender, marking Eastern Front turning point.

questions.questionText: What were Axis Powers?
questions.explanation: Axis Powers united under fascist ideology, conquered much of Europe and Asia before defeat.

questions.questionText: What were the main causes of WWII?

options.text: Treaty of Versailles, rise of fascism, appeasement failure

questions.explanation: WWI Treaty harshness, Nazi aggression, fascist expansion, and failed appeasement caused WWII.

questions.questionText: What was the Blitzkrieg strategy?

options.text: Lightning fast military offensive using tanks and aircraft

questions.explanation: Blitzkrieg combined fast-moving armor, air support, and communications to achieve rapid victories.

questions.questionText: What was the Battle of Britain?

options.text: German air campaign against Britain, defeated by RAF

questions.explanation: Battle of Britain (1940) saw Luftwaffe defeated by RAF, preventing German invasion of Britain.

questions.questionText: What was Pearl Harbor?

options.text: Japanese surprise attack on US naval base bringing US into war

questions.explanation: Pearl Harbor attack (Dec 7, 1941) destroyed US Pacific Fleet and brought America into WWII.

questions.questionText: What were concentration camps?
questions.explanation: Nazi camps imprisoned and murdered millions including Jews, Roma, political prisoners, and others.

questions.questionText: What was the United Nations?

options.text: Post-war international organization replacing League of Nations

questions.explanation: UN created in 1945 to maintain international peace and prevent future wars.

questions.questionText: What role did atomic bombs play in ending WWII?

options.text: US bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki forced Japanese surrender
Had no effect on ending war

questions.explanation: Atomic bombs on Hiroshima (Aug 6) and Nagasaki (Aug 9) led to Japanese surrender.

questions.questionText: Analyze the impact of WWII on African colonies.

options.text: Colonial troops gained experience, saw contradictions, accelerated independence

questions.explanation: African troops fought for freedom they saw denied at home, sparking independence movements.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the moral implications of the atomic bombings.

options.text: Debated as necessary vs. unjust targeting of civilians

questions.explanation: Atomic bombings remain controversial - some argue necessity, others condemn civilian targeting.

questions.questionText: How did WWII change the global balance of power?

options.text: Europe weakened, US and USSR emerged as superpowers, decolonization accelerated

questions.explanation: WWII devastated Europe, making US and USSR dominant while inspiring colonial independence.

questions.questionText: Analyze the role of women in WWII.

options.text: Entered workforce, supported military, challenged traditional gender roles

questions.explanation: Women filled factory jobs, supported war efforts, and gained economic independence.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the legacy of the Holocaust.

options.text: Created international human rights law, Israel's founding, memorial culture

questions.explanation: Holocaust led to Genocide Convention, human rights frameworks, and global memory culture.

questions.questionText: How did WWII influence civil rights movements?

options.text: Highlighted hypocrisy of fighting fascism while segregating at home
Had no connection to civil rights

questions.explanation: African Americans pointed out irony of fighting Nazi racism while facing American segregation.
